newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg/mark seen capped at 3.0150 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg/mark seen capped at 3.0150 marks.

text.p: Sterling is poised to hold above 3.0 marks in Europe after a sprint higher but it will remain well capped around the 3.0150-mark area, said chartists.

For cable, which sank to its lowest in more than seven weeks to $1.6203 on Wednesday, further upside momentum is expected after it managed to recover above a long-term support trendline cutting in around $1.6250, said chartists.
"Sterling/mark has been volatile. It is now neutral and should aim to consolidate," said Nico Bakker, technical analyst at ABN AMRO.
At 0735 GMT sterling/mark was trading at 3.0120/30.
This compares to 2.9890/00 marks in late Europe Wednesday.
Chartists said sterling was looking to consolidate after skidding on Tuesday to lows of 2.9735 marks.

With sterling's conquest of the 3.0-mark barrier, chartists said it could attempt further upside ground but will remain well capped around the 3.0140/50 level, representing peaks reached early on Thursday.
Sterling's upside momentum, however, would be confirmed if it manages to hold around the 3.0140/50 level in late dealings.
"There is no clear picture for stg/mark but there is good support around 3.0050/60," said Bakker.
Below that, analysts said the pair would remain constructive as long as it managed to hold above support at 2.9840/60 and 2.9800 marks.
Below that, analysts said a long-term upward trendline, dating from around July 1996 and cutting in around 2.8400 marks, would provide hefty support.

Cable was robust on the charts after bouncing off 7-1/2 week lows around $1.6203 on Wednesday. Chartists said it was poised to push higher after managing to recover above a long-term supportive trendline dating back to March 1996.
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 57 pct, Stg/dollar: 35 pct --Julia Meehan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6701
